promptAsSent:
Use the image_gen tool to generate exactly one image, then stop. Do not write files, run commands or edit anything.

Attached reference images, in order:
Image 1: INPUT 1: the swatch layout to paint (layout authority)
Image 2: INPUT 2: the same ship already painted: the finish to match (material only)

Use case: texture map generation / material swatch sheet for a 3D model.
INPUT 1 is a layout sheet of flat-coloured squares on a plain flat mid-blue background. Each square is one hull material of a single 3D spacecraft (a battle-worn pirate Wolf-class frigate), to be painted as a flat, square-on texture sample of that material, in reading order:
first square: deep, slightly dull crimson armour enamel;
second square: warm mid-grey painted machinery steel;
third square: the recess and machinery material, near-black dull steel.
INPUT 2 is the SAME ship, already painted: it is the finish to match. Use its paint colours, sheen, fine seams, fasteners and its even battle wear. Never copy INPUT 2's composition, view or shapes.

Paint each square as a texture swatch of its material. Each square will be cut out and tiled many times across the model's small fittings, so:
- Keep the squares exactly where they are, the same size, with the same plain blue gutters between them. Do not zoom, crop, shift, rotate, enlarge or shrink anything. Each square is filled edge to edge with its material, right up to its straight edges, with nothing drawn outside it; any empty slot stays plain blue.
- Each square is a flat, seen-square-on sample of hard-used industrial plate: a fine, even, all-over surface. Only sparse, small detail: a few thin plate seams and small scattered fasteners, even fine chipping and scratching, a thin even film of grime. The detail is small and evenly distributed over the whole square, with no single dominant feature: no large rivet rows, no seam or panel line across the middle, no hatches, panels, grilles, labels, stripes or markings, nothing centred.
- Keep each square's colour exactly: crimson stays deep crimson, grey stays warm mid-grey, near-black stays near-black. No colour changes, no repair patches, no different-coloured plates.
- Wear is even across each whole square. No rust, soot, scorch marks, burns, impact damage, dents, holes, large stains or any concentrated area of wear.
- Lighting: flat, even, shadowless, like an albedo/diffuse texture map. No cast shadows, no ambient-occlusion darkening, no specular highlights, no reflections, no vignette, no directional light, no gradient across a square, no bright border or chipped edge line round a square.
- Background and gutters: the same plain flat uniform mid-blue as INPUT 1, with no floor, shadow, text, labels or borders.
Output: one landscape 16:9 image, same composition as INPUT 1.
